customer_zen: Hey team — we're seeing intermittent 403s when streaming with SSE from the hosted API. Happens after a few chunks (~10–30s). Sample trace header we see: req=6f5a2c81 region=us-west-2. Tried curl from our infra and from laptop, behavior differs. Can you help gather a minimal repro?

jamie: Thanks — can you paste the exact curl you used and the raw response headers (with -i)? The X-Request-Id / x-rw-request-id values are most helpful. Also which token type (user or service) and whether you have edge proxy in front?

customer_zen: Pasting what we used (sanitized):

```
curl -v -N \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi...<snip>...qU" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"hi","stream":true}' \ 
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=open-rl"
```

Response: first run 200 with SSE chunks, second run gets 403 after initial comment chunk. Header we saw on 403: `x-request-id: 6f5a2c81` and `x-rw-err: auth.invalid_token`.

jamie: OK — quick checklist:
- Re-run with `-i` to capture headers, and `-v` to get TLS/handshake logs.
- Try `--http2 -N --no-buffer` on curl to avoid libcurl buffering.
- If you have a proxy, run from a machine that bypasses it (or show proxy headers).
- Capture the server `x-request-id` and the exact `x-rw-err` value and paste both.
- If token is short-lived, include what time you issued it (hour + timezone).

sandeep: Also ask: are you rotating tokens automatically? We had a customer where token refresh TTL briefly overlapped with validation window and edge returned 403 mid-stream. If you can share the token issue timestamp (or a token prefix like `eyJ...qU` first/last 4 chars) that helps correlate.

arya: One more useful capture: run curl with `--trace-ascii /tmp/curl.trace` so we can see the raw TLS frames and any 401/403 body returned before the SSE cut. If possible dump the headers to a file `-D headers.out`.

support-bot: Automated note — if this becomes an escalated debug bundle, please attach `headers.out`, `curl.trace`, and any client logs (send timestamps) to the ticket. Use `/support create-bundle` to generate the upload link.

customer_zen: OK, trying the recommended minimal capture now. Question: is there any special header your auth gateway expects for streaming vs non-streaming? We only set Authorization and Accept.

jamie: No special header required. If you're behind a proxy that rewrites `Connection` or strips `Authorization` on upgrade/keepalive, that can cause mid-stream 403s. Add `-H "Connection: keep-alive"` explicitly for a test. Also include `-H "x-rw-client: prod-frontend"` or similar so we can see your client id in our logs.

customer_zen: Ran these 3 tests from laptop (no proxy) and from CI (behind proxy). Laptop: consistent 200 streaming. CI: 403 after ~12s. Attached headers.out from CI run (pasted minimal):

```
HTTP/2 403
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
x-request-id: 6f5a2c81
x-rw-err: auth.invalid_token
date: Tue, 09 Apr 2024 16:34:12 GMT
```

Also included `curl.trace` excerpt showing a short `HTTP/2 403` frame.

jamie: Great repro. Next steps for us: eng will look up `6f5a2c81` for that time window and cross-check gateway logs for token validation. Meanwhile can you try one quick validated minimal curl we can use here to reproduce from CI (replace token):

```
# Minimal: keep-alive + http2 + raw headers
curl --http2 -N -v -i \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  -H "Connection: keep-alive" \ 
  -H "x-rw-client: ci-pipeline" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=open-rl"
```

Please paste the `x-request-id` you get and upload `headers.out` + `curl.trace`. If CI is failing and laptop passes, the likely culprits are (in order): proxy rewriting/stripping auth, TLS session reuse differences, or token refresh window.

sandeep: On our side: we'll search auth gateway logs for `6f5a2c81` and correlate with token validation service logs for the timestamp you provided (2024-04-09T16:34:12Z). If we find an auth error pattern we'll post back with exact cause.

arya: If you can, also run a quick curl from a different external IP (mobile tether) to rule out any IP-based rate limiting.

customer_zen: Running minimal now from CI + will share artifacts. Thanks — will update shortly. :thumbsup:
